title: [TASK] Rebuild documentation for implementers, verification developers, integrators, and managers
body:
## Objective / problem

Rebuild the current Milan FPGA documentation around four reader paths.

- Implementation developer
- Verification developer
- System integrator
- Project manager

Current pages must use short prose, focused diagrams, and verified facts.
HDL timing must use editable WaveDrom sources.
Obsolete pages must move into `docs/history/v1/`.
The public tree must use the neutral term `test device`.

## Evidence / motivation

Observed:

- `docs/README.md` presents topics, not audience paths.
- Current prose contains long paragraphs and long sentences.
- Historical pages remain mixed inside current documentation directories.
- The repository has 321 Markdown, RST, or AsciiDoc files.
- Four pinned submodules need one clear integration map.
- WaveDrom tooling exists but lacks complete reader guidance.
- Verification spans Python, C, and C++ ownership boundaries.
- Issue #247 previously scrubbed the private peer name.
- The user requested this documentation redesign on 2026-08-31.

Expected:

- Readers select a role and follow a short path.
- HDL behavior has small, verified timing diagrams.
- Test developers understand Python, C, and C++ responsibilities.
- Historical pages are visibly separated from current authorities.
- Documentation remains mechanically checkable.

## Authoritative references

- `AGENTS.md`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `REQUIREMENTS.md`
- `docs/README.md`
- `docs/DOC_GENERATION.md`
- `.github/workflows/docs.yml`
- Issue #247
- User documentation directive dated 2026-08-31

Normative requirements remain authoritative.
This Issue cannot silently change technical behavior.

## Context entry points

Read first:

- `docs/README.md`
- `docs/overview/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `docs/overview/SYSTEM_DOMAIN_MAP.md`
- `docs/fpga/FPGA_DESIGN.md`
- `docs/testing/TESTING.md`
- `docs/testing/RUNNING_TESTS.md`
- `tb/verilator/README.md`
- `tests/README.md`
- `.gitmodules`
- `scripts/docs_check.py`
- `scripts/gen_wavedrom.py`

Expand only through verified implementation dependencies.

## Scope

In scope:

- Audit current documentation against implementation.
- Inspect every pinned submodule.
- Document submodule purpose, pin, and boundary.
- Create four audience entry paths.
- Separate implementation and verification developer views.
- Map Python, C, and C++ test responsibilities.
- Add focused Mermaid diagrams.
- Add focused WaveDrom HDL timing diagrams.
- Keep editable diagram sources.
- Document diagram regeneration.
- Move genuinely obsolete pages into `docs/history/v1/`.
- Preserve archive provenance and successor links.
- Repair links and indexes after moves.
- Preserve the neutral test-device wording gate.
- Add focused checks for new documentation rules.
- Publish an audit and unresolved-conflict list.

Out of scope:

- RTL behavior changes.
- Firmware behavior changes.
- Submodule pin changes.
- Editing content inside pinned submodules.
- Reinterpreting normative requirements.
- Replacing generated evidence with prose.
- Deleting historical evidence.
- Merging without maintainer authorization.

## Executor

[A0] documentation executor

## Independent reviewer

[R1] Cleared-context reviewer, with external review still mandatory

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/README.md` offers four audience paths.
- [ ] Implementation developers receive a focused guide.
- [ ] Verification developers receive a focused guide.
- [ ] Python, C, and C++ responsibilities are explicit.
- [ ] Every submodule has purpose and boundary documentation.
- [ ] Every recorded submodule pin matches Git.
- [ ] Important HDL transactions use WaveDrom.
- [ ] WaveDrom sources are editable and reproducible.
- [ ] Mermaid diagrams explain architecture and workflows.
- [ ] New current-guide prose uses ten words maximum.
- [ ] Code, commands, paths, tables, diagrams, and quotations are exempt.
- [ ] Current prose uses bullets and short paragraphs.
- [ ] No tracked documentation exposes the private device name.
- [ ] Current documentation uses `test device`.
- [ ] Obsolete pages move under `docs/history/v1/`.
- [ ] Archived pages carry status and successor metadata.
- [ ] Current indexes exclude archived authorities.
- [ ] Internal links remain valid.
- [ ] Generated documentation remains reproducible.
- [ ] Documentation facts match implementation.
- [ ] No functional source behavior changes.

## Validation

Commands:

```sh
python3 scripts/docs_check.py
python3 scripts/docs_check.py --selftest
python3 scripts/check_feature_status.py --self-test
python3 docs/traceability/gen_module_matrix.py --check
python3 scripts/check_doc_paths.py
python3 scripts/check_archive.py
python3 scripts/gen_toc.py --verify-anchors
python3 scripts/gen_toc.py --check
python3 sw/builder/test_builder.py
python3 scripts/check_baremetal_only.py --check
python3 scripts/check_baremetal_only.py --selftest
```

Also run every new focused checker.
Regenerate every changed diagram.
Inspect every rendered WaveDrom PNG.
Run the complete docs workflow replica.
Run repository gates required by `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

Expected result:

- Every command exits zero.
- Generated files show no drift.
- Negative controls prove new checks can fail.
- The review records all five required lenses.

## Dependencies / lane conflicts

Related completed work:

- #94 documentation hygiene
- #98 documentation consistency
- #247 private peer scrub
- #259 retired product-path cleanup

Potential conflicts:

- Active lanes touching documentation indexes
- Active lanes changing test entry points
- Active lanes changing submodule pins

Reconcile current `origin/dev` before every broad move.
Do not edit another lane branch.

## Open design/specification decision?

No. Scope is settled and may become Ready.

## Decision details

- Mermaid owns structural diagrams.
- WaveDrom owns HDL timing diagrams.
- Historical evidence moves, never disappears.
- Submodule content stays read-only.
- Technical conflicts become separate public decisions.
- Sentence checks target new current guides.
- Existing normative documents remain unchanged unless inaccurate.

## Discovered from

User documentation audit and redesign request, 2026-08-31.
